teaser.text: Ferguson Enterprises Inc. is a distributor of the equipment and materials that keep buildings, factories and water systems working. It makes money by putting the right products, expertise and delivery close to the professionals who install and maintain them.

stock.title: Ferguson stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Ferguson stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash conversion, valuation, and the risks that could change the path.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast puts Ferguson’s share price at $265.04 in October 2027 and $324.21 in October 2029. It hinges on project shipments turning into collections, inventory and receivables releasing cash, and leverage moving toward the level at which buybacks resume.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Ferguson’s business works, how its rivals compare, how management is executing, and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could Ferguson’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast puts Ferguson’s share price at $265.04 in October 2027 and $291.44 in October 2028. It reaches $324.21 in October 2029.
The bear case has a 27% probability. The base case has a 53% probability. The bull case has a 20% probability, making gradual recovery the central expectation.

blocks.heading: What could go right or wrong for Ferguson?

paragraphs.text: The base path assumes recovery toward roughly 9% reported margins as existing operations improve and FloWorks contributes. The bear case gives $2,850 million, then $2,950 million and $3,100 million because housing weakness, delayed projects and integration costs persist. The bull case gives $3,400 million, then $3,750 million and $4,100 million because infrastructure, industrial demand and cross-selling lift both volume and margins. The base remains closest to management’s mid-single-digit sales outlook and normalized margin history.

The bear case assumes housing and discretionary renovation remain weak while industrial and infrastructure projects slip. FloWorks adds sales but not enough profit or cash to offset financing and integration costs. The price reaches $218.10 in October 2027 and $210.37 in October 2029. Its 27% probability reflects the possibility that weak demand, working-capital pressure and higher leverage arrive together. The June quarter’s cash shortfall makes that risk material.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Ferguson really make?

paragraphs.text: Fiscal 2025 shows the difference. Operating cash flow was $1,908 million, and free cash flow after capital spending was $1,603 million. Ferguson’s own free-cash-flow figure also included asset-sale proceeds, while acquisitions remained a separate use of cash. Stock compensation is another economic cost that a stricter cash analysis may deduct.

blocks.heading: How much does Ferguson pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend rises from $3.65 to $4.42 per share in the base case. That extends a five-year record of annual increases from $2.39 to $3.32. The bear case freezes at $3.48 because first-half free cash flow was $482 million against $347 million of dividends. The bull case reaches $5.05 as stronger cash conversion permits faster increases.

blocks.heading: Does Ferguson's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: That is what happened in the strongest payout years. Ferguson used balance-sheet capacity to support dividends and buybacks, including an exceptional distribution connected with the UK sale. A buyback pays shareholders to surrender shares; reducing the share count can raise earnings per share even if total profit barely changes.

Fiscal 2025 shows the difference. Operating cash flow was $1,908 million, and free cash flow after capital spending was $1,603 million. Ferguson’s own free-cash-flow figure also included asset-sale proceeds, while acquisitions remained a separate use of cash. Stock compensation is another economic cost that a stricter cash analysis may deduct.

paragraphs.text: For the year to December 2026, management guides to mid-single-digit sales growth and a 9.5%–9.8% adjusted operating margin, excluding FloWorks. It expects $200 million of interest expense and $375–$425 million of capital spending. The guidance uses a 26% adjusted tax rate. Its medium-term ambition is more than $40 billion in revenue and more than $4 billion in adjusted operating profit. The target margin is above 10%.

blocks.heading: Has Ferguson kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Ferguson has sensible measures and evidence of reducing its share count, but shareholders should ask whether the award adjustment was a one-time repair or the beginning of negotiable performance targets. That is the clearest answer to whether management is on their side: the structure points toward alignment, while discretion remains the risk.

blocks.heading: How has Ferguson's revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose from $8,363 million in June 2025 to $8,751 million in June 2026. Operating income rose from $842 million to $893 million, while diluted EPS rose from $3.21 to $3.43. The progress was genuine, but reported operating-profit growth benefited from lower restructuring charges. Adjusted operating profit grew only 2.9%.

blocks.heading: What should Ferguson watch in the next release?

paragraphs.text: The first check is revised guidance. Ferguson should distinguish growth from the existing business from growth supplied by FloWorks, and explain the related interest and integration costs.

The second check is cash. Higher project activity can require more inventory and customer credit before it produces collections. A reassuring result would connect shipments with cash receipts and explain the remaining stock investment. More orders alongside slower collections would keep the financing burden high.
